races.name: Zyn Frontrunner EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Zyn Strong Stride EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Date Line
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly has the clearest tactical advantage here — a 2-from-2 record on similar Good going with Callum Shepherd up, and uncontested control of a three-runner mile is a potent combination, though her 420-day absence is the single most significant risk factor in the race.

runners_data.name: Evening Call
runners_data.note: Harry Davies partners this Haggas-trained filly whose going suitability is entirely unknown and whose natural midfield tendencies leave her last of three throughout, meaning she is entirely dependent on the pace being honest enough to close into — her lightly-raced status adds intrigue but not reliable form evidence.

runners_data.name: Gilding The Lily
runners_data.note: The Gosden yard's prominent racer brings 7f all-weather form into this turf mile, and Robert Havlin's tactical intelligence over Newmarket's straight makes her the most natural beneficiary if Date Line's return from a lengthy layoff sees any weakness in the final furlong; last run just 14 days ago is an advantage in freshness terms.

races.paceDynamic: Date Line is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of three and will lead from the outset on Good To Firm ground at Newmarket's July course, a track that rewards horses who can dictate and control tempo over a mile. With Gilding The Lily tracking prominently and no serious challenger for the early lead, Date Line will face zero pressure through the first half and can set whatever tempo suits Charlie Johnston's team, making this a truly uncontested lead. Evening Call, redistributed to the rear in the mapping, is naturally more of a midfield type and will be last of three throughout, relying on Date Line setting a pace that ultimately flatters those coming from behind. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — Date Line controls every variable and Gilding The Lily can slot in a perfect stalking position, while Evening Call must hope the pace is strong enough to reel in two horses in front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Date Line Leads, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line dictates an uncontested, metronomic tempo and quickens when asked in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Date Line's 2-2 record on similar Good going and her 7f form translates well to this mile trip on a flat, galloping track where front-runners who control the race frequently see it out strongly. With no rival willing or able to challenge her early, Callum Shepherd can conserve her energy through the first six furlongs and produce a controlled, professional front-running display that is very difficult to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gilding The Lily tracks Date Line perfectly and produces a stronger finish over the final two furlongs, overhauling her in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Gilding The Lily showed form on the all-weather at Sandown over 7f and Robert Havlin is an experienced hand at timing a prominent challenge at Newmarket, where the July course rewards horses who travel smoothly behind the pace before unleashing a sustained run. If Date Line's long absence of 420 days leaves her slightly short of peak fitness, Gilding The Lily sitting a length or two behind her could have the fresher legs in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough and Evening Call, despite being lightly raced with unknown going profile, unleashes a late run past both rivals.
scenarios.body: Evening Call is trained by William Haggas, whose yard operates at a solid 6/47 over 14 days, and a Haggas debutante or lightly-raced filly appearing here likely arrives well-prepared, but the redistribution to the rear means she must rely on genuine pace being set to close into.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled, All Beaten Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line sets a falsely slow tempo that causes a messy sprint finish with no horse able to assert decisively.
scenarios.body: A crawl would compress the field and reduce Date Line's front-running advantage, giving Evening Call and Gilding The Lily a flat-out sprint from the two-furlong pole, which in a field of only three can produce an unpredictable result where the least-fancied runner's raw speed momentarily matters.

watchPoints.text: Date Line's 420-day absence is the single biggest variable — watch her in the paddock and early running for signs of ring-rustiness or reluctance to stride out on Good To Firm ground, as any physical conservatism from her will collapse her dominant pace scenario.

Evening Call arrives with a completely unknown going and form profile — William Haggas rarely runs unexposed fillies in public without confidence, so her market move or absence of one before the off is worth monitoring closely.

Gilding The Lily's form comes from Sandown's all-weather over 7f, so watch whether she handles Good To Firm turf and sees out the extra furlong at Newmarket — two unproven variables that could undermine an otherwise promising stalking position.

With only three runners, any scrimmage, stumble or interference at the start could disproportionately affect the result — a clean break is particularly critical for Date Line who must establish her lead immediately to dictate terms.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Freight Frenzy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by Good ground with strong course form (sim-going 9/12, 2W5P), steps back to a mile from longer trips recently and the visor headgear is a positive flag; 78 days off is the main query but James Owen's yard is active and he fits the pace shape well.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Fresh off a 12-day turnaround for Patrick Morris, this hold-up horse has been busy at 8f on Good ground and arrives needing a truly run race to close from off the pace; the stable has had a quiet 14-day window (0/8) which tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Calyxoh shaped well enough with a third three starts back and returns in good order on 12 days' rest, handling today's distance and going with experience; winless in recent starts, he nonetheless rates highest of the eight and is the one to beat off 133 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form (form: 446112) with back-to-back wins at 8f on Good ground, this prominent racer is perfectly placed to exploit an uncontested Triggerman-led tempo; Laura Pearson takes the ride and the tight headgear flag is noted.
runners_data.comment: The Sweet Escape arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, and a close second last time out keeps him firmly in form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 131 lb from stall 2 is the chief weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (368974) and, while naturally a hold-up horse, the field's volume of off-the-pace types has pushed the mapping to midfield — the style-fit score of 0.94 reflects genuine positional compromise and tempers confidence; handles Good ground well enough but the trip is a slight stretch.
runners_data.comment: Special Ghaiyyath brings strong fitness credentials having run just 16 days ago, and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 76 marks him out as a live threat from stall one; the concern is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: Handles Good ground and has distance experience at 12f-16f, suggesting stamina is not a concern at a mile, but the horse is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role by the race shape (style-fit 0.91); Michael Keady's yard has been quiet (0/10 in 14 days) and the form string (63-046) offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unplaced effort three starts back and only a fourth two starts back to show recently, Currumbin carries 123 lb from stall four and, ranked last on our figures, makes little appeal despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Triggerman
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front runner for Patrick Morris, he has a clean lead and will set an uncontested gallop, though his recent form (39-680) and zero wins from five Good-ground starts flag modest ability; the 7lb claimer Finlay Bassett takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Triggerman is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going; a well-beaten eighth two starts back and unplaced latest make it difficult to make a case, though 22 days off and a return to familiar conditions offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rising Force
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field (OR 74, 135lbs) and a genuine hold-up horse with a win and place from 8f on Good ground; Marco Ghiani is an experienced pilot but the horse needs the pace to press on sufficiently for his late run to bridge the gap.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out gives Rising Force a live each-way claim, though a fifth and fourth in the two runs before that effort suggest he was some way off it; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs keeps him fresh enough to factor from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid Good-ground course form (sim-going 10/15, 4W4P over 7f) stepping up to a mile, which is the key uncertainty; Harry Eustace's yard is relatively quiet (1/9 in 14 days) but if the extra furlong suits, the position in the race is ideal.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and a winner four starts back, Mr Ubiquitous brings distance and going experience to the table, but his recent form is patchy and carrying 134 lb from stall 8 leaves plenty to prove at a mark of 73.

races.paceDynamic: Triggerman is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's July course mile. Sir Edward Lear and Mr Ubiquitous will press forward into prominent positions just off Triggerman's shoulder, while The Sweet Escape is also a prominent racer who will compete for that same real estate, creating a compact early order rather than a strung-out field. The midfield will be populated by the redistributed hold-up types Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin alongside Rising Force and Calyxoh, who are genuine off-the-pace horses. With one pace-setter and no pressure on the leader, this shapes as a steadily-run affair that culminates in a dash for home, strongly favouring prominent racers who can travel close to the tempo and unleash a kick in the final two furlongs — hold-up runners will need the pace to collapse in front of them, which a lone, uncontested leader rarely delivers. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely sit at the rear and benefit, with Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin redistributed to midfield on the map; of the genuine prominent runners, Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape, and Mr Ubiquitous are best placed to secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Control
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman sets a calm, uncontested pace and the prominent trio of Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape, and Mr Ubiquitous travel smoothly just off the leader throughout.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the front end the race unfolds at a measured tempo, and when the sprint begins from two furlongs out those already in position will have the decisive edge over hold-up horses with ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners push the pace harder than expected in the middle stages, burning off their finishing kicks and leaving the race open for horses ridden quietly.
scenarios.body: Rising Force, Calyxoh, and genuine hold-up types such as Special Ghaiyyath would be the beneficiaries if the leaders tie each other up in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Triggerman Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman's uncontested lead is so comfortable that he conserves enough energy to repel all challengers in the final furlong at this modest level.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground with no rival willing to pressure him early, the front runner could exploit the steady fractions and simply outstay rivals who leave their run too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the straight and horses from deep in the field get a clear, unimpeded run to swoop late.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies on Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin racing effectively out of their natural roles as mapped, making it the least likely shape given their redistribution penalty and the controlled tempo anticipated.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sir Edward Lear or The Sweet Escape pushes forward to press Triggerman — if two prominent types apply pressure the tempo quickens and the scenario shifts from controlled lead to contested pace, opening the door for closers like Rising Force.

Rising Force is the highest-rated horse in the field and, if Marco Ghiani times the challenge perfectly from the rear, the OR 74 mark could prove well ahead of rivals — monitor whether he gets a clean passage from off the pace.

Mr Ubiquitous steps up from 7f to a mile for the first time in this stable's recent quiet spell; if the extra furlong stretches him the prominent position could be a liability rather than an advantage.

Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are both mapped out of their true hold-up roles — if the pace does not collapse in the straight their chances are structurally compromised and they should be monitored for signs of not travelling from further back than usual.

Going is described as Good in the race card but every other race on the card is returned Good To Firm — conditions are likely firmer than the declared going suggests, which could sharpen the tempo and bring forward runners into even sharper focus.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Container Storage Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who won over 6f on good ground 7 days ago, giving Callum Shepherd an in-form angle to exploit; hood and eyeshield combination (hg:/es) suggests a horse that needs settling, and with the front two burning up front the closing run may arrive too late on this straight track.
runners_data.comment: Fifty Nifty bounced back to winning form last time out and, carrying 145 lb from stall two, he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the inconsistency in recent starts is a mild reservation, but on a mark of 70 he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Consistent 7-year-old hold-up type with six of his last six runs over 6f on good ground — a remarkably specific profile for this race — and his last-three form of 3-5-6 shows he is running into form, though Jack Doughty is a 5lb claiming partner that helps offset the weight burden at OR=70.
runners_data.comment: Mumayaz showed his best when winning five starts back, but has failed to recapture that form since, finishing no better than third in his last four outings; he has run over today's trip and going, returns after 22 days, and carries 140 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course-and-distance placed form (2nd on Southwell, 3rd on Good) who gives apprentice Shay Farmer a good tactical chance if the front-runners fight each other; trainer Adam Kirby returns 0/8 in the 14-day window suggesting no special prep, but the horse's style is perfectly suited to a genuinely run race.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat but knocking hard on the door, Ziggy's Condor brings strong recent placing form — second last time out and third two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 77 marking him a leading threat; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed four times in her last five runs at this class, with two wins over the trip on Flat-equivalent surfaces; Dougie Costello brings strong handling experience and her fresh record (8d LR) suits — she repeatedly shows up at distances between 6-7f in the prominent position that suits this shape exactly.
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back and won three starts back, so Spirit Of Jenny clearly has ability, but that eighth last time out is a concern; she has run over today's trip and going, and 138 lb from stall six makes this a stiff ask at a rating of 68.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing a visor (hg:v) who has won over 7f on good ground and placed three times in five recent starts in similar conditions; 13 days since last run is ideal freshness, but Kaiya Fraser's claim needs to deliver clean passage in what is a competitive, pace-driven race.
runners_data.comment: Northcliff finished second last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, with 13 days' rest leaving him primed on fitness; the concern is that he has found only one win in his last six starts, suggesting he can be vulnerable when it matters most.

runners_data.name: Beauzon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose recent form of 1-1-1-6-0-0 tells a story of a horse who wins when he gets a soft lead but fades when the pace is tested; with Romantic Twilight sure to press him hard, his winning form at OR=67 came on Southwell and the jump to Good-to-Firm Newmarket on contested terms is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Beauzon has won three times in his last six starts, showing a clear ability to hit the front, but back-to-back unplaced efforts since dampen enthusiasm; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests freshness, though 137 lb from stall 12 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a headgear flag (hg:p) who has placed five times in nine recent outings including a win on good ground, though his last eight runs include only one top-three finish over 6f; Chloe Lyons's 7lb claim gives a weight relief that slightly flatters a horse whose recent trajectory has been flat.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Path shaped with promise when third last time out and returns on a quick turnaround of just 14 days, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; our rating of 77 marks him as a strong danger, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find more to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Romantic Twilight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner who won over this course and distance on good ground and will clash immediately with Beauzon for the lead; her form line of 1-6-0-9-5 shows she has not recaptured that winning level, and the contested duel may expose her if she is forced to race harder than she needs to across the first two furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Romantic Twilight showed she can win, landing victory five starts back, but has struggled since, finishing no better than fifth in her last four starts. She has run over today's distance and going before, returns after 23 days, and carries 134 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Currahee
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up type wearing a tongue-tie and a hood (hg:tp) who won over 7f on soft going for Stuart Williams — the same trainer who runs Rebel Path in this race, creating a split-stable scenario; his 6f form on good ground (4th, 6th, 9th) is less convincing than his stamina-test wins and 14 days since last run matches his stablemate's prep.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts, with a ninth and eighth in recent starts making him hard to fancy here, and our figures rank him ninth of twelve in the field; the win five starts back offers slim hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: A genuine ten-year-old who has produced outstanding recent form figures of 1-2-2-2-12 on similar ground, but his true racing style is hold-up — he has been placed on the map in midfield simply because the rear-of-field is overcrowded with similar types in this field, and that positional compromise may cost him the late run he needs to execute his best form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 127 lb from stall nine, Bayraat is hard to fancy on the back of an unplaced effort last time out, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner who won over 6f on good ground on her most recent start and is trained by Micky Fenton, a small yard whose 2/3 in the T14 window signals active form; her best form is clearly coming now, and at OR=60 she races off a lenient mark if able to replicate that winning run in more competitive company.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Molly Mac faces a stiff ask against stronger company, but she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, which counts for something.

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist by nature — his form on Southwell artificial surfaces reads well (1st, 8th, 9th, 11th, 8th) but this Good-to-Firm Newmarket surface is a different proposition; placed on the map in midfield due to field congestion at the rear, his 31-day absence and the style-fit compromise both temper expectations even if Phil McEntee has him ready.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Em Jay Kay makes little appeal after four poor efforts in his last four starts, though a win five starts back shows he can find the winning post and he has experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Twilight and Beauzon are confirmed front-runners who will clash for the lead from the off on this straight 6f Newmarket July course, creating a genuinely contested pace that should produce an honest, true-run gallop throughout. Beauzon has won twice on Flat-course surfaces and will press hard for supremacy, while Romantic Twilight — a 3-year-old who led and won over course-and-distance — will be equally unwilling to concede. The resulting pressure from these two means the pace is unlikely to be manufactured or manipulated, suiting those who can travel through the race rather than being dragged along. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are genuine late-runners pushed into a midfield position on the map because the true back of the field is congested — meaning their ability to unleash a finishing run from their natural spot is compromised. This contested pace shapes the race firmly in favour of prominent or midfield horses with proven finishing kicks on good-to-firm ground who can time their challenge off a genuine gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Twilight and Beauzon burn each other off and hand the race to a prominent tracker hitting the line fresh.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fight for supremacy and tie each other up in the final furlong, leaving a prominent horse who has tracked the pace just off the leaders to come through and score. Spirit Of Jenny and Ziggy's Condor are ideally suited here — both prominent-style runners with proven form on good ground over 6f who can pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Romantic Twilight — proves superior in the battle and controls the race enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: Although both front-runners push hard, one establishes a clear advantage by halfway and the pace becomes manageable for the leader, allowing them to conserve enough energy to repel closers. Romantic Twilight, as the younger horse on an upward curve, is the more likely candidate to come out on top of that duel given her course-and-distance win profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Comes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the honest gallop causes the front two to fade simultaneously and the race is run at a tempo that allows a well-handicapped midfield runner to storm through late.
scenarios.body: A strong pace that collapses in the final 100 yards opens a corridor for a midfield horse with a turn of foot on good ground to arrive late and win without being seen. Northcliff, who has won over this course-and-distance condition and races off a handy mark, and Mumayaz, consistent over this exact trip and going combination, are the profiles to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Denied
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Bayraat and Em Jay Kay away from their natural rear positions actually works against them and they cannot execute their hold-up style.
scenarios.body: With Bayraat and Em Jay Kay mapped into midfield rather than their natural rear-of-field positions, neither is likely to get the deep late run they need, and this scenario — where genuine late closers rattle home from well off the pace — is structurally undermined. On the slim chance the pace is fast enough to make it happen anyway, Bayraat's strong recent form figures of 1-2-2-2 on similar going give him the best claims among the redistributed pair.

watchPoints.text: Romantic Twilight and Beauzon are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first furlong closely, as whichever horse gives way first may drop tamely out of contention, opening the race up for the prominent trackers behind.

Spirit Of Jenny has placed in four of her last five starts and races in the prominent position that this pace map directly favours — if Dougie Costello gets her into a rhythm just off the battling front two, she is the shape's most dangerous profile.

Bayraat's recent figures of 1-2-2-2 are elite for this class, but his inability to get his natural hold-up position due to field congestion at the rear is a structural disadvantage — watch whether Rob Hornby settles him further back than the map suggests or pushes forward, as either choice carries risk.

Molly Mac won on her most recent start and drops into handicap company off OR=60 — Grace McEntee has had recent success for the Fenton yard (T14: 2/3) and if the pace bias draws energy away from the front, this lightly-weighted 3-year-old could arrive late with a strong finish.

Northcliff wears a visor for the first time in several runs — headgear changes at Newmarket on a fair-going surface can sharpen a hold-up horse's sectional speed, and if the visor produces an improved reaction through the final two furlongs, Kaiya Fraser's claim makes the handicap weight very manageable.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: God Of War
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 100 days off, which is the most significant flag here; Tom Clover's 5/17 14-day strike rate is workable but the layoff combined with a style that needs genuine pace to close into makes this a low-probability profile in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 100 days, God Of War faces questions on freshness, though he has run over today's distance and going and a rating of 94 offers mild encouragement from stall ten carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with excellent recent course form (3rd and 1st both over 8f on Good at this track), back quickly on 13 days' rest and Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a genuine asset in a handicap off OR 90; tracks leaders effectively and has shown he finishes on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Sterling Knight shaped with promise when third two starts back, but was unplaced either side of that effort and could manage only seventh last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 93 gives him a chance off 137 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who won over this exact course and distance on Good ground earlier this season, a very relevant piece of form; her 70-day absence is a minor concern but Harry Eustace's yard has good form fresh, and she has the profile to benefit if the race develops any tempo at all.
runners_data.comment: Principality won two starts back but has been out of the frame since, and 70 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Legitimate hold-up horse with strong recent form including two wins and multiple placings on Good ground, though he has been operating mainly at 7f — the step back to 8f on his flat record is worth noting; Callum Shepherd rides and the 16-day turnaround from a live showing is a positive flag.
runners_data.comment: Zarathos comes into this unplaced last time out and ranks eighth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights. He does arrive fit on a 16-day turnaround, has experience over today's trip and going, and back-to-back wins four and five starts back show ability, but recent form makes appeal difficult.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent racer with three wins and six places at the highest recent frequency, but in a field saturated with prominent types he is unlikely to settle where he wants to; his chances are tempered by the redistribution — his best form comes when he can control or sit close to the pace rather than being shuffled back.
runners_data.comment: Croupier shaped well when third last time out and that placed effort, combined with his experience over today's trip and going, makes him a leading threat under 135 lb; the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, in headgear, trained by Kathy Turner who has a 1/3 14-day record — small but live; a 3-year-old carrying 125lbs with winning form over this course and distance on Good ground, and with no rivals likely to pressurise him early, his ability to control the gallop makes him a pivotal shape-setter even if his chance of winning is conditional on a very slow pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of ten on our figures, Brocklesby Bill faces a stiff task under 125 lb from stall nine, yet he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives in fair nick with two wins in his last five starts, including a win last time out.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose natural role is hold-up but has been placed in midfield on this map due to congestion at the rear — his actual recent record shows finishes of 4th and 3rd on this course and distance, so there is residual ability; the STYLE_FIT flag means his chance should be discounted if the scenario requires him to operate from a position he won't naturally secure.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Mythical Guest faces a stiff ask here, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement; drawn in stall two and back after 27 days.

runners_data.name: Storm Star
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 95 with Andrew Balding's powerful yard (8/56 14-day) but his recent form is deeply underwhelming — 0 wins in last 15 similar-going runs — and his 57-day break combined with a prominent style in a congested midfield makes this hard to back; needs a significant return to form to feature.
runners_data.comment: Storm Star shaped with promise when second two starts back and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour, but he has been winless in recent starts and the 57-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type with proven winning and placing form over this exact course and distance on Good ground, wearing a hood (headgear), and fresh enough on 20 days' rest; William Carver rides and his form string of 1-6-0-6-1 shows he can produce sharp efforts interspersed with flat runs — the question is which one appears today.
runners_data.comment: Hickory arrives on the back of a win last time out and looks well-placed to go again, handling both today's trip and going with experience to call upon; the main concern is that his recent record shows some inconsistency, with four defeats in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Prominent runner trained by Nigel Tinkler (5/28 14-day) who has been disappointing over this trip on Good ground in recent starts, particularly after a failed experiment at 12f; Rob Hornby's booking is a stable positive but the form string of 0-0-5-5-6 in recent outings and limited course form make this hard to place prominently in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Tuscan Hills has run over today's trip and going before, and a 13-day turnaround keeps him fresh; winless in his last five starts, a fifth last time out at least shows consistency, and 140 lb from stall three gives him a workable weight and draw to build on.

races.paceDynamic: Brocklesby Bill is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse wanting to lead, should be able to dictate a sustainable, unchallenged gallop from the gates — a measured pace on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile at Newmarket's July course. Behind him, a cluster of prominent-style horses — Storm Star, Sterling Knight, Hickory, and Tuscan Hills — will jostle for the favoured positions just off the leader, creating compression and potential traffic issues from the two-furlong pole inward. The hold-up horses God Of War, Principality, and Zarathos will settle in the rear quarter and rely on a strong enough gallop to close on; with Brocklesby Bill not being harassed, the pace may not be truly searching, which risks keeping the rear-section beyond reach. This field contains more prominent-minded runners than can all secure their natural position: Sterling Knight and Hickory — with course form and finishing consistency at this track — are best placed to actually hold prominent berths, while Croupier and Mythical Guest, both tagged as redistributed, are unlikely to operate from their preferred ground. The race shape tilts clearly in favour of prominent-to-midfield runners who can track the leader into the straight and produce a sustained finish, rather than late-closers who need genuine pace injection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent chasers settle smoothly, the winner emerges from 2nd-4th turning in.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill bowls along at a regulated tempo, and the horses immediately tracking him — Sterling Knight and Hickory — get the dream draw into the final two furlongs without expending energy in traffic; on Good to Firm Newmarket ground, this shape consistently rewards horses who travel prominently and quicken off a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is even slower than expected and the prominent pack fails to close, Brocklesby Bill or the lead-section horse sustains to the line.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill, uncontested and travelling comfortably in his headgear, simply never gets reeled in as the hold-up horses are stranded with too much ground to make up in the straight; the Good to Firm surface rewards a relaxed, low-energy leader who hits the rising ground fresh.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack becomes squeezed rounding the Dip and the race fractures, hold-up horses with clear runs emerge late.
scenarios.body: Principality or Zarathos, both operating on their best ground and at a suitable trip, find daylight inside the final furlong as a bunched prominent group interferes; Zarathos brings strong recent form (1-1-2 in last three wins at this trip and going) and Principality has already won over this course and distance this season.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up, True Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected prominent horse attempts to pressurise Brocklesby Bill early, lifting the tempo enough to set up a genuine staying finish.
scenarios.body: A faster-run race opens the door for hold-up horses to close with purpose, but this scenario requires redistributed types like Croupier or Mythical Guest — neither operating from their natural position — to force the pace, making it the least likely shape to materialise; if it does, God Of War's hold-up profile and solid form on this going gives him the strongest residual claim.

watchPoints.text: Brocklesby Bill's uncontested lead is the pivotal pace lever — if he bowls along unchallenged at a moderate gallop, any hold-up horse including Principality and Zarathos may find the race simply doesn't set up for them.

The cluster of four prominent horses — Sterling Knight, Hickory, Storm Star, and Tuscan Hills — all wanting to sit 2nd-4th creates a high probability of crowding and interference approaching the Dip at the 2f marker; any horse caught in that pocket risks losing a winning position.

Croupier and Mythical Guest are both operating away from their natural running positions due to field congestion — if either ends up in unfamiliar territory in the first half of the race, they could cause unexpected interference with the horses genuinely around them on the map.

God Of War is returning from 100 days off and represents a significant unknown quantity in terms of fitness; if he comes on the bridle unexpectedly he could be a live player, but the layoff in a race not set up for hold-up horses makes him an unreliable anchor for any scenario.

Storm Star's top weight (142lbs) and Andrew Balding's strong overall stats are eye-catching but his 57-day absence and zero wins in 15 recent similar-going runs mean any bold show from him would likely signal something visible in pre-race paddock inspection — worth watching how he presents.

races.name: Racing Welfare Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead from a true hold-up profile — the key pace-setter by default in this race — but has won twice at 16f on good ground and showed consistency in his last four runs, so the role may suit more than his style tag suggests; the 21-day break under apprentice Owen Lewis (5) for Roger Teal who has had only one winner from ten in the last 14 days is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, mark Rogue Empire as a serious threat, and he returns fit on 21 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that ninth last time out leaves a question mark over his current form.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old veteran of 2m good-ground races with one win and three places from fifteen similar-going runs, he is the natural hold-up type who knows how to travel through a race; blinkers applied, John Berry stable has been quiet (0/5 T14), and he arrives 21 days fresh — Catton will likely aim to sit just off the pace and pounce.
runners_data.comment: Tarbat Ness bounced back to winning form two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with 21 days since that unplaced run leaving him fresh enough to fire again; the concern is whether he can bounce back sharply enough from that latest blank.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form — 2-3-2-3-2 in his last five over 2m on good and standard ground — marks him as the standout in-form runner; his true hold-up style is shifted into midfield by the crowded rear, which tempers confidence slightly, but Jack Jones' runner (1/13 T14) under apprentice Dickson has genuine claims if getting a clear run from two out.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and clearly in fine nick after a run 13 days ago, An Bradan Feasa has placed in three consecutive outings and gets the better of his rivals on our rating; he has run over today's trip and going before, and the 138 lb burden is the sole reservation.

runners_data.name: Mio Amico
runners_data.note: A 94-day absence is the most significant flag here — his form before that break included a win and a place at 14f on standard ground, but he has no proven record on good or fast turf, and his zero wins/places from thirteen similar-going runs is deeply concerning; nudged into midfield from his natural hold-up position, Alfie Redman (7) faces a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and with a speed rating of 56 that does little to inspire, Mio Amico faces a stiff task after 94 days off, though he has run over today's distance and going before and does boast two wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Four wins and seven places from eleven outings on similar going — the strongest going record in the field — and a visor fitted, Laravie has been highly consistent at 2m+ including wins at 17f; James Owen has been extremely busy (9/45 T14), and Paetel will likely try to position closer than Laravie's natural rear-running style allows, making the redistribution less of a handicap than for others.
runners_data.comment: Laravie arrives just 13 days fresh off a third, with two seconds and back-to-back wins deeper in her recent form, and experience over today's trip and going standing her in good stead; the risk is that she has not converted in her last two starts.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a serious concern at 2m on fast ground where the final climb at Newmarket finds out those who don't truly stay; one win from seven at this track/going combination and arrives just ten days after his last run — Ian Williams (4/40 T14) keeps him busy, but the finishing profile is a red flag in a staying heat.
runners_data.comment: Free World won last time out and comes back on a quick ten-day turnaround, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures and officially rated just 60, he faces a stiff task against better-rated rivals; the experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no surprises.

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins (16f good, 14f standard) and a second make this Tony Carroll runner one of the more progressive profiles in the field; lightest weight at 122lbs is a genuine advantage in a handicap, the hood is applied for focus, and Carroll's strong recent record (5/47 T14) gives stable confidence — naturally a hold-up type nudged into midfield, but that position may actually suit over 2m with apprentice Coppins (5) able to claim further.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last six starts, including a victory last time out and a second two starts back, The Craftymaster arrives on a pleasing run of form; however, he carries 122 lb and our rating places him fifth of seven, suggesting he faces a stiff ask here.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Empire is the lone confirmed front runner in this 2m Good to Firm apprentice handicap, redistributed to the lead having shown genuine prominent tendencies, and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front with no rival likely to challenge for the early lead. The pace will be honest but controlled — a lone, unpressured leader over two miles on fast ground typically produces a steadily-run race where the tempo builds through the second half, suiting those who can travel through the race rather than those who need a true breakneck gallop to finish off rivals. With the vast majority of this field being genuine hold-up types forced into a midfield cluster — An Bradan Feasa, Mio Amico, Laravie, Free World and The Craftymaster all redistributed from their natural rear-of-field position into midfield — the race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handy and produce a sustained late run rather than a sharp, tactical burst. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; of those, Laravie and An Bradan Feasa are the most likely to naturally secure a position closer to the pace given their consistent form at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rogue Empire Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Empire is allowed to dictate an uncontested, comfortable gallop throughout and the pack behind fails to close the gap until too late.
scenarios.body: Rogue Empire sets a measured pace, conserving energy on the Good to Firm Newmarket straight, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers once the race quickens in the final quarter mile; the hold-up pack, forced into a congested midfield group, finds too much to do against a relaxed leader who has timed it perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Rogue Empire is genuinely strong enough through the final mile to stretch the field and open the race up for those finishing powerfully.
scenarios.body: An Bradan Feasa and Laravie, the two most capable hold-up runners in the field with strong recent form at 2m on good ground, pick their way through the midfield cluster and sustain their runs to overhaul a tiring Rogue Empire; this scenario is partly tempered by the redistribution of these horses out of their natural rear position, meaning they may not get quite the clean run a true hold-up type would.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Suits Craftymaster
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and the race becomes a stamina-sapping grind in the final furlong where lower-weighted, in-form stayers have an edge.
scenarios.body: The Craftymaster, carrying the lightest weight and benefiting from a hood, has won twice at 2m on similar ground and thrives when races turn into tests of endurance; a steadily-run contest that only quickens late plays to his progressive profile and his ability to sustain effort over the full two miles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Closers Swamp Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Empire fails to see out the trip or overcooks the fractions, leaving the entire field in a position to swoop.
scenarios.body: Mio Amico and Free World, despite being redistributed from true hold-up positions and carrying the concerns of a 94-day absence and a fading-finish flag respectively, could benefit if the leader hits a flat spot dramatically; however, this shape carries the lowest probability precisely because the horses best-placed to exploit it are not operating in their natural race position and their form at the trip on this surface is the weakest in the field.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Empire sets the entire race shape — watch whether Owen Lewis allows him to bowl along or tries to anchor him early, as either extreme changes every other runner's positioning in a field with no natural pace to fill the vacuum.

An Bradan Feasa's wide draw and midfield redistribution means Jake Dickson must find a clear passage turning into the Newmarket straight — if the hold-up cluster closes up, he could face a wall of horses at the critical moment.

Laravie's visor is new headgear — watch for an early positive reaction as Mason Paetel may be instructed to ride closer to the pace than usual to exploit it, which could fundamentally alter the race dynamic if she gets a prominent pitch.

Free World's fading-in-finish tag over 2m on Good to Firm is a structural concern — Ryan Kavanagh must decide whether to commit early or conserve, and if he overcooks the first mile, that flag becomes a near-certainty in the home straight.

The Craftymaster's 122lb weight advantage over the top weights (138lbs) is 16lbs — in a stamina contest at 2m on fast ground where the race truly tests, monitor whether that allowance proves decisive in the closing stages.
